What is deforestation?
questions.a: Felling of trees over large areas for farms, roads, housing, timber and industry.

questions.q: Name two natural and two human causes of deforestation.
questions.a: Natural: forest fires, drought. Human: clearing land for agriculture, use of wood for fuel and furniture.

questions.q: How does deforestation harm the water cycle?
questions.a: Fewer trees mean less transpiration and rain, more floods and soil erosion - the local climate dries up.

questions.q: What is desertification?
questions.a: Fertile land slowly turning into desert after its tree cover is lost and soil erodes.

questions.q: Why does cutting forests raise the amount of CO2 in air?
questions.a: Trees absorb CO2; with fewer trees, more carbon dioxide stays in the air, adding to global warming.

questions.q: Name one effect of deforestation on wild animals.
questions.a: They lose food and shelter, so many die or must move, pushing species toward extinction.

questions.q: What is a biosphere reserve?
questions.a: A large protected area where wildlife, plant and human life are conserved together, like the Nilgiri or Nanda Devi reserve.

questions.q: How does a biosphere reserve differ from a sanctuary?
questions.a: A biosphere reserve is bigger and also allows limited human activity in zones; sanctuaries mainly protect animals.

questions.q: Name one famous biosphere reserve of India.
questions.a: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (also Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Pachmarhi).

questions.q: What do the terms flora and fauna mean?
questions.a: Flora is the plant life of a region; fauna is its animal life.

questions.q: Give two examples each of Indian flora and fauna.
questions.a: Flora: sal and teak trees; fauna: tiger, peacock (also bison, orchids).

questions.q: Why must we keep records of flora and fauna?
questions.a: Records show which species are common, rare or vanishing, guiding conservation plans.

questions.q: What is an endemic species?
questions.a: A species found only in a particular region and nowhere else, like the Siberian crane in cold wetlands or sal and wild mango in India.

questions.q: Why are endemic species at greater risk of extinction?
questions.a: They live in one place only, so habitat loss there wipes out the whole species.

questions.q: Distinguish endangered from endemic species.
questions.a: Endangered species are close to extinction anywhere; endemic species are restricted to one area (they may or may not be endangered).

questions.q: What is a wildlife sanctuary?
questions.a: A protected area where wild animals live safely, with killing, capturing or poaching forbidden.

questions.q: Name two well-known wildlife sanctuaries of India.
questions.a: Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary (Keoladeo) and Jaldapara sanctuary; also Ranthambore and Periyar.

questions.q: Can people visit a wildlife sanctuary?
questions.a: Yes, for study and tourism under rules - unlike national parks, sanctuaries allow limited human use.

questions.q: What is a national park?
questions.a: A reserve large enough to protect whole ecosystems - habitat, plants and animals together, with human activity nearly banned.

questions.q: Name two national parks of India.
questions.a: Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand) and Kaziranga (Assam); also Gir and Kanha.

questions.q: What is an ecosystem?
questions.a: All plants, animals and microorganisms of an area together with their surroundings, functioning as one unit.

questions.q: What is the Red Data Book?
questions.a: A record of endangered and rare species of plants and animals, kept so they can be watched and saved.

questions.q: Who maintains the Red Data Book?
questions.a: IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) maintains it internationally; India keeps its own lists.

questions.q: Why is the red panda in the Red Data Book?
questions.a: Its numbers are falling fast due to habitat loss - it is an endangered species needing protection.

questions.q: What is migration? Give an example.
questions.a: Seasonal movement of animals between habitats - the Siberian crane flies to Bharatpur each winter; Arctic terns migrate pole to pole.

questions.q: Why do birds migrate?
questions.a: To escape harsh weather and find food and safe breeding grounds.

questions.q: How do migratory birds find their way?
questions.a: They follow landmarks, the sun and stars, and the earth's magnetic field.

questions.q: What is reforestation?
questions.a: Planting new trees to rebuild a forest on land that lost its forest cover.

questions.q: How is reforestation different from afforestation?
questions.a: Reforestation replants a forest where one was cut; afforestation grows forests on land that never had them recently.

questions.q: Suggest two ways to conserve forests.
questions.a: Ban illegal felling and involve local people in tree planting (like Chipko); use paper and wood sparingly and recycle.
